You never were, Grampa.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Aw, I'd hug ya, but I know you'd just get embarrassed.
Grampa! I don't mind when you spit at home, but I have to work with these people.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Aw, jabberjack! Schoolhouse don't put out spittoons, I ain't responsible.
Wrinkly gibberish?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Back then, I was known as Sgt. Simpson, and I commanded the Flying Hellfish -- the fightingest squad in the fightingest company in the third fightingest battalion in the army. And we were all from Springfield. There was Police Chief Wiggum's father, Iggy Wiggum...
Yes, sir. I will.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Bart's got a problem with a local young bully named Nelson. I thought you could help him with some kind of strategy.
KBBL is gonna give me something stupid!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Bart, I'm having palpitations.
I glanced at it... boy cries "wolf"... has a few laughs... I forget how it ends.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Bart, is that light green?
I begged him to stop, but he said it was for the good of the nation.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Big deal! When I was a pup we got spanked by presidents 'til the cows came home! Grover Cleveland spanked me on two nonconsecutive occasions!
When are Mom and Dad coming back?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Bored, are ya? Lisa, go cut me a switch.
Five seconds to slip-off. And four, three--

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Boy? What are you doing up here? Also, what am I doing up here?
Oh, he's not bothering me any more. Buck McCoy helped me.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Buck McCoy? He was the greatest of them all. He was bigger than opium!
Me and Nelson were best friends, and now I think he's gonna kill me!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Bully problems, eh? You know, they say all bullies are cowards. It's not true, they're brave 'cause they're strong.
Oh, this is great stuff -- I can pad it out to ten pages. Goodnight, Grampa.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: But I'm not tired!
No, I'll be good!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: But my favorite pub is still there.
No. Even she thought it was crap.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: But what you did wasn't for nothin'. It was the best two weeks of this final, horrible part of my life.
I have to go.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: California, here we come!
After a pulse-pounding race, hypertension pills win again!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Call me crazy, but I can't stop betting on dementia.
He knows what he's doing.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Can't get a good sarsaparilla like this back in Springfield. It angries up the blood.
Thanks lady.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Dear Advertisers: I am disgusted with the way old people are depicted on television. We are not all vibrant, fun-loving sex maniacs. Many of us are bitter, resentful individuals who remember the good old days when entertainment was bland and inoffensive. The following is a list of words I never want to hear on television again. Number one: Bra. Number two: Horny. Number three: Family jewels.
Yo, Grampa! Time for the awards.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Did you call the girl from the escort service?
Come on. You were in World War Two.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Do you know how I survived D-Day?
I don't feel so good. Can you take me to the hospital?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Finally, we're doing something I wanna do.
Look, if you're going to stay in my room, could you at least stop making up gibberish?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Gibberish, eh? Then what's this?
You all stink!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Glamorous Godfrey is dead.
Sure. That was twenty minutes ago.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Gonna be in the tub for awhile.
I don't get it, Grampa. If you guys like all that boring stuff, why did you follow me out here?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Gotta do something 'til bingo.
What do you have against Santa?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: He screwed me over back in Double-ya Double-ya two. I was a Navy pilot in the Pacific...
Sure, here you go.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Hey Bart, leave some of that bad attitude for the ring.
You're great at a party, Lisa. Really great.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Hey you, no, shut that door! Stop it! Put that away! No, stop, oh!
Okay. I can handle that.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Hey, give me a slice!
Do we let her spend the rest of her life in the wild? Or let her die in captivity, like Grampa?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Hey, in my mind I'm free!
Where's my elephant?!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Hey, they're playing the elephant song.
Not without the keys, he isn't.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Hey, you got the keys!
No way! They're finally having some fun!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: How low can I go?
Hey, stop shaking the harness.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: How low can I gooo...
What are you doing?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I ain't a heel no more -- I'm a good guy... and you're a baby-face.
I gave him a caramel. He should have been chewing for hours!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I couldn't unwrap it!
Didn't you wonder why you were getting checks for doing absolutely nothing?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I figured 'cause the Democrats were in power again.
I'll never trust another old person.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I fooled you. So long suckers. Hee hee hee.
Game's over, Grampa.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I got down on the floor for this?
Well, I'm sure you'll make up something. Maybe you just need more of my classmates around.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I gotta hole up here for awhile. They might still be after me.
Grampa, I need some advice. Did you ever have a crush on an older woman?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I had a crush on the oldest woman. One hundred and twenty years old, she was. Here's a picture of her delivering Eubie Blake.
Face on a mountain!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I hated the Roosie-velts and all them family dynasties. The Kennedys, the Bushes, Jon Voigt and Angelina Jolie, Mayor Daley and his smart ass son, the Daily Show.
Yeah, so we've already heard stories from thousands of years ago, about stuff that didn't happen.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I have an important announcement to make. I've had a lot of time to think since my hands got too shaky to play cards...
Well... you are the first thing I took care of that didn't die.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I hear that a lot.
This won't even cover the vig on what I owe!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I lost the rest investing in a Broadway musical based on the real life story of Eddie Gaedel, the midget who had one big league at-bat.
So how do you know so much about American history?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I pieced it together, mostly from sugar packets.
There, there, you'll be fine. I'll take care of everything you need.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I want a foot rub!
Dad, why'd you shut our dog in a cabinet?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I'll answer that: your father's an idjit!
We flushed the gator down the toilet, but it got stuck halfway and now we have to feed it.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I'll bet you want a piece of me. Well, you ain't gonna get it, see! Ha, ha, ha...
It's not a threat if I don't know what it means.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I'll fix your wagon!
Man, I must really love him.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I'm not gonna die today.
Grampa, you're the spaceship, not the...

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I'm the what? I thought I was this guy. Ohhh.
I'll say. Wasn't it great? And the question mark leaves the door open for a sequel.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I've seen that movie ten times and I never get tired of that ending.
Nah, I know enough.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I, myself, played in this ballpark, back in nineteen forty-deuce. That was during the war, when sushi was called "liberty logs," and no one had ever heard of it.
Okay, she's gone. Let's break out of here and have some fun!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: If I get up, somebody'll take my chair.
Hey, Grampa, do you think your dead buddies get up and walk around at night?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: If they're anything like me, they have to get up twice. Okay, hold up here.
Consarn it, he's getting away!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: In a pig's eye he is!
I want to avenge you, but I don't know how.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: In my younger days, I was an ace crime fighter -- the "Crimson Cockatoo!
It was his idea.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: In that case, I'll have a whiskey sour.
To Krusty. The greatest entertainer in the world. Except maybe that guy.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Is this the bus to the Civic Center?
Well, if you saved Burns' life, why does he want to kill you?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: It was the closing days of the war. We had just flushed some Germans out of an abandoned castle...
So Grampa, not like I'm anxious to go, but I've been here ten minutes, which is like seven hours in kid years...

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: It's her! The little girl who doesn't recoil at the sight of us.
Just what I was gonna say.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Look at me! I'm actin' young! Woooow!
I'm gonna take stuff from the lost and found!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: My feet hurt! My left ear's freezing! My right ear's burning! I got fish smell in my wrinkles!
Great story, Grampa. Coulda used a vampire, though. 'Night.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: My own grandson thinks I'm a liar.
Grampa, Matlock's not real.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Neither are my teeth, but I can still eat corn on the cob if someone cuts it off and smushes it into a fine paste. Now that's good eating.
I was supposed to be in charge of you. I can't let Mom and Dad know what I did. But I promise I'll take good care of you until you're well again.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: No deal! I'm gettin' outta here!
Quick Gramma, hide!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: No door is gonna keep me from my meddlin'! Stand up straight, Bart.
Is that her?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: No! Wait, it was the second one.
--sixty-four times. No more, no less. Got it.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: No, no. Sixty-three times if you're out of air. Sixty-four is if you found the treasure.
Yes, but do you need one?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Nobody needs one! Now start rubbin'!
Oh, there's gotta be something to do around here. Hey, are they pulling the plug on anybody today?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Nope, everybody's paid up.
No way, this is our rec room!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Not anymore! I already put my posters up!
Keep my dog? Till when?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Not too long, just till we die.
To the antique store!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Now, what can I do for you? Eat something green? Vote for someone brown?
Oh, please, no.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Now... hey, listen! Now, my story begins in 19-dickety-two. We had to say "dickety" 'cause the Kaiser had stolen our word "twenty." I chased that rascal to get it back, but gave up after dickety-six miles.
Here's your new plate, Grampa.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh boy! There's crumbs on it!
A copy of Radioactive Man number 27. That's the first time he fights Dr. Crab. Then I wanna buy that baseball card where the guy is flippin' the bird.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh yeah, I've seen that one.
Psst! Grampa! I think this guy's a little nuts.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh yeah? Well, General George S. Patton was a little nuts. And this guy is completely out of his mind. We can't fail!
Why is she saying all this? Is she dying?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, she's just upset 'cuz I told her her brain's turnin' to mush. You know, on account of the Simpson gene.
Now we can get the treasure!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, what's the use? Burns would still find some way to take it from me.
I don't know... Fleecin' old people?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, why not? If we don't take their money, they'll just give it to some televangelist.
No way, José.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Okay, we've seen a lion. Can we go now?
Hey Grampa, we got a letter for Gramma.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Open it up! This may be my last chance to invade her privacy!
Look, Grampa, I'm fine! I really don't need any more home remedies.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oral thermometer, my eye! Think warm thoughts, boy, 'cause this is mighty cold.
Yours.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Quitcher bellyaching about Marge and let me read the paper.
Yeah, why would you play chess through the mail when you can play chess through the internet, or preferably, not play chess at all?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: See here, sass mouth, you're not too big for me to tan your hide!
What happened?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: She fell in with that Guinness Book of Records crowd. Suddenly, she didn't have any time for me. I wore a 15 pound beard of bees for that woman, but it just wasn't enough.
Ow!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Skeeter bites are good luck. Scratch it and you get a wish.
Yes.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: So do I. But I get back to sleep by counting the men I let down. There's Jerry, Izzy, Brooklyn, the O'Donnell boys, the lost ship: P.T.-108, the Poor Buggers of Meatloaf Ridge, the Andrew sisters...
That's my dog, man.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: So long, lamp. Now stop loafing, and help your Grampa unpack.
Dumpster.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Sorry to crowd ya, boy, but I'll let you in on a secret. Burns is after me 'cause he wants the Hellfish Bonanza.
Ow!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Sorry, Bart. You can push them out of a plane, you can march them off a cliff, you can send them off to die on some God-forsaken rock. But, for some reason, you can't slap 'em. Now, apologize to that boy right now.
Either the grave or somewhere much worse.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Sour cream and chives? In my day, all we put on potatoes was pine needles and barber hair! I hate this century!
Really? Did that ever work for you?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Sure did! I remember it like it was yesterday...
There comes a time to beat the crap out of childish things!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Sure is a hard way to catch a mouse.
Can we borrow this, Grampa?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Sure, she still works.
Can I tag along?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Sure, why not? School ain't helpin' ya.
Fine. How's it goin'?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Terrible -- I got this new roommate and he won't stop yappin'!
Oh, Dad, this is the best birthday I've ever had.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: That doll is evil, I tells ya. Evil! EEEVIL!
Ah, Grampa! Woo!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: That was the first time I ever saw "Itchy and Scratchy" and I didn't like it one bit. It was disgusting and violent. I think all you people are despicable. For shame!
Grampa, why don't you tell us a story? You've led an interesting life.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: That's a lie and you know it. But I have seen a lot of movies...
But I'm so pretty.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: That's for others to say now.
Wow!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: That's my old Smith & Wesson. If you're gonna play with it, be careful, 'cause it's loaded.
There it is!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: That's the glitziest "Welcome To" sign ever.
Quiet, Dad, or we'll have to throw you outta here.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: The pictures... they're coming... alive!
So I kinda like this girl at school but I'm not sure if she likes me back.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: There's one sure way to find out if a girl likes you -- steal a kiss!
What are those, Grampa?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: These are hobo signs. They're to tell other hobos if a place is friendly or not.
You know it, Glamorous. Eye gouge, ear bite, folding chair, hair pull, face-fart, flying face-fart, and then I start fighting dirty.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: They're gonna hate you so much.
They're cheering, Grampa.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: This is what I've been missing my whole life.

So the substitute teacher comes in and says her name is Mrs. Doody. And everyone's looking at me like "Take it, Bart. Run with it". And it hits me: I've become a clown... a class clown. And it sickens me.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Three wars back, we called sauerkraut Liberty Cabbage, and we called Liberty Cabbage super slaw. And back then, a suitcase was known as a Swedish lunchbox. 'Course, nobody knew that but me.
First let's slap on some Band-Aids so they feel really bad for ditching us.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Time to find a woman who needs some TLC... a tired liver-spotted coot.
Grampa, Mom was in such a hurry, she forgot to give you this. It's a list of the things Lisa and I can and can't do.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Uh huh.. Uh-huh... You're allowed smoke cigars?
You have a story with an ending?!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Uh-huh. All my stories have endings now. They're putting something in my Jell-O down at the home. Anyway, Homer and that dog went together like Christmas and suicidal thoughts.
It's Captain Bringdown and the Buzzkillers. If you're gonna make your move, you better do it quick.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Wait! Stop the music!
Uh-oh, here comes a Xylon cruiser. Whoa, whoa, whoa! Go into hyperspace! Ready, hit it!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Wait. Where's the Hyperspace?
Hey, Grampa. Aisle six and step on it.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well, all right, but put out that cigar.
Mmm-hmm. You bossed around the richest, most powerful guy in town. How come you were a sergeant and he was only a private?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well, he got busted down for obstructing a probe from J. Edgar Hoover. And we got stuck with him...
Grampa, everyone's callin' me a coward.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well, join the club! Anyone who makes it to old age has got to be part coward.
I need some advice, Grampa. See, there's this bully at school who keeps beating me up.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well, let me tell you something, boy. If you don't stand up for yourself, bullies are gonna be picking on you for the rest of your life.
Is that story true, Grampa?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well, most of it. I did wear a dress for a period in the forties. Oh, they had designers then...
Wow, that sounds pretty sweet.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well, there is a price. You wake up sweating in the middle of the night?
Thank God your mental powers haven't deteriorated.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well, why the hell am I down here?
Full speed ahead! Damn the torpedoes!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: What did he say? Put on our tuxedoes?
Oh and the

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: What the hell is that?
Finish the damn story. I've got a hockey game tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: When I finally got back to the house...
I met the new principal, Mr. Baumgartner. He seemed really cool. When he walked through the gym, he shot a basket!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Who has disturbed my tomb?
Grampa, quick, tell me everything you know about World War One!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: World War One? I fought in that. Course, to enlist, I had to lie about my age...
Huh? Oh. I sure did... Here's a bus schedule.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Wow! Fits right in my pocket!
Oh, great. I specifically asked not to be seated next to a baby.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Wow, we must really be flying high. Those people down there look all tiny and blurry... just like the inside of a cataract.
Wow, he did.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Yeah, in the Depression, you had to grift. Either that, or work.
Hey, Grampa. Stealing Mom's car?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Yeah, it's the only way to win back Zelda. And if I go to prison, I'll get better food and more hugs.
... move your joystick to the left.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Yes, move the... what's a joystick? You didn't tell me...
Holy Hannah! I've got more muscles than a New England clambake. Now all I need is a superhero name.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You can be the Crimson Cockaboy. Hmmm?
Gay wedding. But I can get you in.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You can? Is there an open bar?
Honest Abe, can I pin him?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You know it, Laddie Liberty!

I can't believe you, Grampa. The sergeant in that story you told would never be scared of a dork like Burns! You gotta get that treasure! You gotta do it for Ox and Asa and Griff and Burnsie... Well, not so much Burnsie.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You really think I can do it?
School? Oh my God, I've wasted the whole summer. There's so many things I still wanna do.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You think you're behind.
Gotcha. Hey, Grampa, do you think I could've been a Flying Hellfish?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You're a gutsy daredevil with a give-'em-hell attitude and a fourth-grade education. You coulda made sergeant.
Look at that hunk o' junk.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You're ignorant! That's the Wright Brothers' Plane! At Kitty Hawk in 1903, Charles Lindbergh flew it fifteen miles on a thimble full of corn oil. Single-handedly won us the Civil War, it did.
Hey Grampa, we need to know your first name.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You're making my tombstone!
Sir, we're gonna bring you back to your retirement home.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Relax! It's just my back...and my hip...spinal column...
What a shame. Not a looker in the bunch.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: So, you workin' tomorrow at the home, Bart?
Egad, man, how are we supposed to pass the time?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Best bet is to stake yourself out a good spot at the starin' window...
Little help?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Boom! Boom, it went! Boom! Just like that! They took a photo of my keister for Stars & Stripes. At least they told me it was for Stars & Stripes.
Say, sport, mind if I have the next dance?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Don't sneak up on a...
Would you ever consider throwing your wig back into the ring?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Go back to being a villain? Forget that! Being hated is the worst feeling there is.
Who told y--?! Yesss. Well, I'd say you were an angel, but angels don't dance like that.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Goodnight, Mrs. Bouvier... Wherever you are.
No need for the blown gasket, Charlie! I'll have her back in one piece.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Grrr. That big ape thinks he can muscle in on my girl, does he? I'll show him. I'm gonna give him the frowning of a lifetime.
That's exactly the poi-- Oh, Simpson, can't you go five seconds without humiliating yourself?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: How long was that?
Agh! Don't kill me!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I ain't gonna kill ya. That'd be cowardly. Monty Burns cowardly. I just wanna watch you squirm.
What are you doing, Godfrey! You're a villain, not some bullet-brained rail-splitter. Without someone to hate, there's no excitement, no thrill!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I don't care! My grandson's soul is at stake!
Fear not, Smithers. I'll move Heaven and Earth to save you! It's still easier than teaching a new assistant my filing system.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I just wish we could make one last big score. But we could never drive past the border patrol.
Well, last night, I had a visit from three spirits...

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: I wish this show had a visit from three new writers.

dialogue.text: It was the heyday of pro wrestling. You could make good money if you were the manly mixture of strong and fat we called beefy.
Now, why don't you stay for dinner.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: It would be my pleasure... son.
Gee, Dad. Way to hog my last moments.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Just a quick game of hacky-sack.
It's too late for me, Marge! Sell the jeans and live like a queen.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Just taking Maggie for a stroll.
Ow. I guess people have some sort of "moral objection" to our sex-drug.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Lemme sell it, you idjit.
Pfft. It wouldn't have made a difference.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Lights out, you punk kids!
Dad, what are you doin' here?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Looking for my teeth.
Now, Marge, just remember, if something goes wrong at the plant, blame the guy who can't speak English. Ah, Tibor, how many times have you saved my butt.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Maggie, your baby-sitter's here.
I'm sorry she rejected your "I'm Sorry," cake, but in a way, I'm not. I guess what I'm trying to say is I like cake.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Marge, don't feel bad. You did what any parent would do.
Well, we need help. Someone who can make money with a bar that has no customers and zero charm.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Moe, you shipped yourself here?
I know what you're up to, Mayor Terwigajer. And no one in my family's gonna stand for it!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Move your god darned house, Son!
Hey, watch the movie.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Movies were better in our day. For a nickel you got two movies, a cartoon, a bag of popcorn, and a whuppin'. Kept your mind on your business.
Hey, my dad was lousy and I didn't sue him. I just dumped him in the cheapest home I could find.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: My IV is empty and my catheter is full!
Eh, they'll be fine.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: No! They're helpless without a greeting -- look at 'em.
Dad, am I cute as a bug's ear?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: No! You're homely as a mule's butt!
I'm a screw-up. I burned down our house.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: No, I'm a screw-up. I burned down our house.
Because it's the honorable thing to do?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: No, because you'll never do any better. You lucky bum! The fish jumped right in the boat. All you gotta do is whack her with the oar.
Are you done?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: No, not yet. I was voted the handsomest boy in Albany, New York.
Well, Happy Birthday, Bea. She can come with us. Hey, there's room for all your friends in the car.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: No, she's not invisible, you idiot. See, it's her birthday tonight.
Oh no! Dad's lost his hearing.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: No, you idiot. I'm ignoring you. You made me miss the last precious moments of Bea's life. I'll never speak to you again.
Me! Me! I want him every night, and forever and ever! 'Cause I love my--

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Nose in a funny book, how rude! Ain't ya never heard of conversation?
Maybe he's thinking of a new shape for the football.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Not so tough when someone hits you from behind with a golf club, are ya?
Dad, we've never been too close, have we?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Not to my knowledge.
All right, that's it, pull over.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Now don't you worry. Just sit back and relax to the smooth sounds of Tommy Dorsey's All-White Orchestra.
Let's dust a few fossils.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Now, this scam was in "The Sting Part II," so nobody knows about it.
The next day, we started auditioning for Chief Wiggum's replacement...

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: OLD MCDONALD HAD A FARM / EE-I-EE-I-O / AND ON THIS FARM HE HAD A CHICK / SWINGINGEST CHICK I KNOW / WITH A WIGGLE WIGGLE HERE AND A WIGGLE WIGGLE THERE...
So this guy might be my real father, and his name starts with "M". Moleman? Mr. Burns? M. Night Shyamalan? That would be a twist worthy of his increasingly lousy films!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Of course I'm your father -- here, mush up your face and you look just like me.
Don't worry, Dad. We'll get out. America is the New York Yankees of countries -- powerful and respected until the year two thousand.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh son, you know how I love a good analogy.
Dad?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh thank God it's the right place. I burst into four homes before this one.
Dad, I don't need advice, I need $15,000 to buy a home.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh! Well, all I own is this house, that I built with my own two hands.
Look what I got for you, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, Hom... gimme the keys.
Tennis court, eh...

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, I can't believe we went through all that, just to wind up with a tennis court.
How you doin', Dad?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, I can't complain and I never do! Thanks for lettin' me live in your guest house.
Your present is leaving.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, I don't see a cab.
NOW, WHAT YOU GOTTA DO / IF YOU WANT TO GET A KISS / IS ACT REAL SMOOTH / AND MAKE YOUR MOVE LIKE THIS.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, I see. SO IF I TAKE YOUR ADVICE / AND MAKE YOUR PATENTED MOVE / THEN MY CHANCES FOR LOVE / WILL SLIGHTLY IMPROVE?
A boy who gets some on the side.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, baby! Now you're free to come back to me!
We leave you the kids for three hours and the county takes them away?!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, bitch, bitch, bitch.
Look at that picture!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, for cryin' out loud.
You're already in a home.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, how could you?
About Virgil.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, right. Well Lisa, Mabel knew her husband well, so she had cooked up a little "payback pie...
Huh uh.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, son, I love you, too. Hey, how about a hug?
Eh, I guess I'll walk home.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, son, I'm glad to see ya. I went for the morning paper and I got lost, and...
My old man. Well, I gotta go.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, son, no. We've got a lotta catchin' up to do. What do you say... we go fishin'?
Enfeebled?! Oo, I know just the guy! Be right back.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, son, this monkey's gonna change my life.
I said "fine." What is it about the word "sure" you don't understand?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, thank you, son.
Lisa, you promised they'd be miserable. What the hell's goin' on?!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, the pharmaceutical man come by! And he shot us full of Christmas cheer!
All right, all right. Young man, since you broke Grampa's teeth -- he gets to break yours.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, this is gonna be sweet.
That's the way Max Power is, Marge. Decisive, uncompromising, and rude.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Oh, wait a minute. The family name is my legacy to you. I got it from my father, and he got it from his father. And he traded a mule for it. And that mule went on to save Spring Break...
Oh, yeah.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Ohhh, son, don't overreach. Go for the dented car, the dead-end job, the less attractive girl. Ohh, I blame myself. I should have had this talk a long time ago.
Listen, Wrinkles! If you know something that'll cheer up my little girl, you'd better spill it. Or I can make things very uncomfortable for you.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Okay, I'll talk! D-Day is June 6th! Repeat: June 6th! Allied forces will land on the beaches of Normandy in the following order: Utah, Omaha, Gold, Juno... are you writing this down, Fritz?
Oh, can I come?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Only if you're ready to stare danger in the face, put your manhood to the ultimate test, and take--
I warn you: I don't know what's in there but if it's about a Simpson, you ain't gonna be proud.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Our ancestors were kicked out of Australia!
What is it, Da --

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: P.U.! Not that close! Ish. Homer, that heart attack made me realize that I'm going to die someday.
Wow, get a load of that toilet.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Please go back! You can make it my birthday present.
Well, we're not going out to help him. We have no idea what hideous creatures might be out there!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Please let me in!
Oh, yeah.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Poor Homer. This world was never meant for one as beautiful as you.
Really? I thought it was Lisa with a beard of bees. Well whatever, brace yourself.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: President Lincoln! You've come back, and you got rid of that hat -- you've got my vote!
Really? Well, that's great, Dad. How can I ever repay you?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Punch that orderly who takes sips out of my juice.
You'll be a bonehead. Come on.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Put it all on forty-one. I've got a feeling about that number.
Bart! How many times have I told you not to bite your sist... Wait a minute! You are a vampire.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Quick! We have to kill the boy!
Okay, okay. I'll be nicer to the dude. I've just never really been a dog person.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Really? What about Bongo?
But I can't ask Mom. She's on the run from the law.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Serves her right fer bein' a sixties radical. Though she was a demon in the sack.
So, Dad, what kind of stupid idea did you put in Lisa's head?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: She wants to steal a kiss, like Pyramus and Thisbe.
Lisa doesn't borrow my car and stay out all night with some... hoochie.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: She's no hoochie. Her name is Zelda and she understands me.
Straight up, Marge. That hoochie only likes you because you can drive.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Shut up! You don't know her! Zelda loves me! I HATE THIS HOUSE!
Come on, Dad. Let's get outta here.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Slow down, boy. What's your hurry?
That's it, a plane!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Smuggle drugs in a plane? That'll never work!
It's found footage!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: So what! We could use another winner in this family.
Why does everything I forbid always happen?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: So, Beautiful, you got your moves memorized?
Drugs! Various drugs! Be sure to read instructions! Uh-oh! Where'd I put the instructions?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: So, who's next? I've got pills to make you sleep late, coagulate, eliminate and copulate. In that order.
Okay, mountain-climbing supplies: rope, ice axe, heart medicine...

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Son! Don't go up that mountain! You'll die up there! Just like I did!
Ah, big deal. Who needs his money? We're gettin' by okay.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Son! You've gotta help me! I hit three people on the way over here, and I don't have any insurance. So, hows 'bout you?
Ah, grrrreetings!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Son, it's me! I floated up toward heaven, but got lost along the way!
Oh my God! This counts as exercise? I'm barely moving and I'm smelling Cinnebun. Sometimes you have to wait till you're thirty-eight to discover who you really are. I'm a seventy-nine-year-old man!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Son, welcome to the club.
Dad! Please, you gotta quit while you're ahead. You understand that, take all your money and leave now.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Sorry, boy, I have to get enough to help everybody.
What have I told you about comical entrances?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Sorry. But you never said anything about comical exits!
Aw, Dad, you've done a lot of great things, but you're a very old man now, and old people are useless. Aren't they? Aren't they? Huh? Yes they are. Yes they are...

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Stop it! It's a form of abuse!
Don't worry, I got it!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Sure is hell to have your husband around all the time, ain't it?
Mind if I take him for a ride?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Sure, I'll just stand here.
So what's the pitch, old man?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Team up with me, boys, and we'll go for the biggest honey pot of 'em all.
All right, brain, you don't like me and I don't like you. But let's just do this and I can get back to killing you with beer.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Thank you for this award. It is a tribute to this great country, that a man who once took a shot at Teddy Roosevelt could win back your trust.
Is she having an affair?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Thanks for asking me to lunch.
Actually, it wasn't me. It was my Dad, Grampa.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Thanks, son. So you see old people aren't so useless after all. Molloy's old and he outsmarted the lot of ya. And I'm even older and I outsmarted him.
Your whole life, you never said one nice thing to me.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: That's 'cause you're a screw-up.
Y'ello. You want my opinion on current movies?! Well, first of all, they're all perfect. Also: when's the Cap'n Crunch movie coming out? And will it be "R" or "Hard R"?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: That's it. It's time for me to die. I'll just get mad about one thing in the newspaper, then go.
This place is in Ireland?!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: That's right. Now let's make our reservations.
You're welcome, honey.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: That's the activity room. We're not allowed in there. That's the library. Not allowed in there, either. And don't even think about going in the game room...
N -- -- yes. But please don't you say that word.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: That's the house you grew up in, Son.
Call me when you get a karaoke machine.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: That's the second time he pulled the plug on me.
Oh my God, I'm late for work.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: The Swedish are coming! The Swedish are coming!
Oh, no, I'm not... Oh, well, let's see whatcha got here.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: The pink ones keep ya from screamin'.
Barney, where's my car?!!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Then prove it. I want you to charm the next pretty young thing that walks through that door.
I still wanna see it.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: There is no hippo!
Ow!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: There she is, the old Radiation King. You'd park yourself right there and watch for hours on end.
F. Murray Abraham.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: There's a rest area. Pull over.
Oh Dad, you and your imagination.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: There's something I think you should know. Homer, you have a half-brother.
Oh, you have a job?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: They pay me eight hundred dollars a week to tell a cat and a mouse what to do.
Great. I'll go shoot myself for bringing this up.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: This is the hippie commune your mother ran off to when life with me became a living hell.
Every year the gulf between rich and poor nations gets larger. Yet, the IMF insists on unrealistic debt-repayment schedules.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: This show stinks. I knew my son would blow it. Where's the remote?
All right! That's it. We're goin' home. I'm sick of you and your stupid tonic!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: This tonic's caused me nothin' but trouble. You've done all the damage you're gonna do!
Oh yeah -- we better "grump it up.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Three dollars for a cup of coffee?! In my day it cost you a dime and they gave you back a quarter!
No wait! I know where the burglar is!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: To the retirement home!
Yes, I do.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Too bad. You ain't getting it.
Sorry, Dad. You're too old.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Too old! Why that just means I have experience. Who chased the Irish out of Springfield Village in ought four? Me, that's who!
Dad, I'm in love.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Uh-oh. Why don't you grab yourself a beer, boy.
C'mon, Lisa. No one in this family is being left below.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Wait for me! I'm a-comin'!
Pass the bug juice, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Wait your turn, you pig. I have an announcement to make. I have decided to give Bea's money away. There are people who really need it. I'm gonna let them come to me and plead their case, and then I'll decide who needs it most.
That's what I was gonna call it!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Wait, I can't go in there grinnin' like a Swede on payday -- it'll rile up poor Lisa if she knows I'm still poppin' that smiley-pill.
I'm afraid I did something to make Marge and the kids leave me.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Wait, I know someone who can help ya -- a doctor who helps people dig up old memories.
Marge, that's what I bought it for!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Watch it with that thing! My skull is eggshell thin!
He's still my dog!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: We got him years ago...
Never went fishing, or played catch, or even hugged each other.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: We never danced the Hoochy-Koo, either. What's your point?
You keep thinking that!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: We're here -- and it's a good thing too. The car's been drivin' funny since Orlando.
Oh, I just love it here. So many things, and so many things of each thing!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Welcome to Sprawl*Mart! Can I get you a cart or a basket?
Aw, Dad, I could kiss you.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well kiss me right here. It's the only part that still has feeling.
So are you gonna say something nice now?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well, I hadn't thought that far ahead.
Dad, I don't have the right words to say how I really feel about you, but at least I know how to beat up a guy who does.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well, at least you never tried to kill me.
I guess I always dreamed that my father would grow old alone.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well, nerts to both of ya! Our love is so strong, not even a thousand crazy schemes could tear it apart!
Brown? No. Orange? No. Elm? Rake? Guessing?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well, well, look who's strollin' down Alzheimer Avenue. You used to know everything about that wife of yours. Even wrote a song about her.
Oh Dad, I got you some scotch. One of those fancy ones the checkout lady had to unlock the cabinet to get.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well, well, well -- look who decided to visit me twice in one year.
You? No way. It's too dangerous.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well, you're no angel behind the wheel. What about your D.U.I.?
And I don't think you're boring. It's just that in today's multi-channel environment, you have too many great choices. Look at Sunday night. There's like eight amazing shows. None of them on Fox.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Well... when you put it that way... all right. I can't say all is forgiven, but most is forgotten.
FALL ON YOUR KNEES / OH HEAR THE ANGELS' VOICES /

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: What a voice. Young Homer is going to make me a millionaire.
Got him! Uh-oh.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: What am I not invited to this time?
Dad, we're canceling the rest of the play.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: What play? What the hell are you talking about?
I'd reached step one: She knew I existed. The only problem was, she didn't care.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: What's the matter, boy?
It's okay, Dad. We know the truth, and we love you.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: What?! The contents of that locker are my private business! Get out!

According to this chapter book, we have a secret weapon: "Evictee will be granted a stay of eviction if said household includes a resident aged sixty-five or over." Finally, a practical use for my father.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Wheee! I'm gonna live like a human in a real house!
Ah, come on, Marge, you're way too...

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: When I was young, toys were built to last! Look at this junk! It breaks the first time you take it out of the box!
Hello, boat store? I'd like to order a boat. What do you mean, dial tone?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Where'd you learn that trick? In the Army?
I learned from the master.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Where's Maggie? Where's Maggie? I'm not kiddin'-- I can't see! My retinas have detached again!
Dad, how come you never gave me any encouragement? Maybe I could've been something more than I am, like a travel agent to a great scientist, or the inventor of a hilarious refrigerator alarm.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Who are you to complain? You lock me up in a home and give me the same damn shower safety seat every Christmas!
I got it, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Why I married you I'll never know.
Dad, I have a problem.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Why'd you come to me. I don't know nothing. I used to get by on my looks. Now they're gone -- withered away like an old piece of fruit.
Dad, do you know what you were kissing? Do you? Do you?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Yeah, I know who I was kissing, and I also know why! I'm a little shaky on when and where, but I got my theories!
I'm going to find my brother. I don't care what it takes. If I have to move heaven and earth, I'm going to find him!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Yeah, right. Good luck.
Aw, Dad... We've got what people never get, a second chance.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Yeah, there's so many things we can...
Wow. Let's go find that hot dog tree I planted.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Yeah, we lived here till the bank foreclosed in sixty-three. Farm went bust after the cows started givin' sour milk. Somethin' musta spooked 'em good.
So, have you figured out who gets the money?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Yes, Homer, I have.
You pay Lenny and Carl to be my friends?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: Yes, but Barney's yours for nothin'.
Don't interrupt! I just thought it would be nice if we shared an interest.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You Korean girls know what a soldier likes.
If you don't start making more sense we're gonna have to put you in a home.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You already put me in a home.
Your memory bubble and you.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You come to me for help rememberin'? That's like asking your horse to do your taxes, which I did back in nineteen ninety-eight.
I'll bet you didn't see that comin'.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You don't care what happens to me when I die.
Oh, no. I'm not giving you my car. You'll probably drive it.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You don't trust your old man? You ungrateful milkshake.
Bart! Forgive him, Dad. He's just a stupid little kid who says the first thing that pops into his head. But, you know, there's wisdom in his innocence.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You don't want it.
Hey, what happened to the bubbles?

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You good-for-nothing jellyfish! While you were lyin' here soakin' like a buncha dirty dishes, I was lonelier than Estes Kefauver at a meeting of "Murder, Incorporated.
Nothing.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You haven't said boo all night, and usually I have to wrestle the bucket out of your greasy mitts.
Sorry, Dad. I was afraid the dragon wouldn't cough the moon back up.

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You idjit! The dragon always coughs the moon back up!
If those kids can forgive that train wreck of a father, then maybe I can forgive...

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You quit drinkin', like a coward! The one thing you were good at!
What?!

dialogue.speaker: Grampa Simpson
dialogue.text: You think I'm boring, and you never visit me, and I got sick of waitin' for ya! So I got a job and found a new dump to live in and I didn't tell you about it, so at least that way I know you're not coming!
